statement: Proved recursive gap lemma: for pairwise coprime q_i and local allowed sets A_i of sizes d_i, the CRT product set A has forward covering radius W(A)<=min_sigma sum_{j=1}^m (q_{sigma(j)}-d_{sigma(j)}) product_{ell<j}q_{sigma(ell)}. For Erdos 451, increasing prime order yields n_k<2k+1+(k+1)P_k/p_max=(1/2+o(1))P_k=exp((1+o(1))k).
dependency_gaps: The proved bound retains the full exp((1+o(1))k) scale and therefore satisfies none of the campaign promotion conditions.
The stronger density-scale CRT interval-box gap lemma G(A)<=q_max^B*C^m*Q/product d_i remains unproved; finite exhaustive and random searches are falsification evidence only.
Minkowski and Dirichlet bounds are symmetric and do not preserve the required coordinate orthant, as the exact k=7 mixed-sign example shows.
Density, translated moments, and additive energy do not control a distinguished or maximum gap without a new interval-product inequality.
The unconditional prefix agreement lemma controls exact coordinate collisions, not interval-membership collisions, and therefore does not imply the gap lemma.
A least-positive-representative theorem is insufficient because the 451 CRT box has trivial representatives in (k,2k]; an exp(o(k)) proof must bound the successor after 2k or the maximum cyclic gap.
The exact recursive loss is the last step Q_{m-1}(p_m-d_m), asymptotic to P_k/2; a new multi-seed pointwise incidence lemma is required to replace it.

The phase-blind short-window projection, conditional-discrepancy, and collision-energy candidates all have exact counterexamples already with one old aligned 451 prime; their loss must depend on block count and Q mod p coherence.
A proved one-prime phase-aware discrepancy lemma records the exact rational-rotation phase sum, but actual successive products can have Q mod p=+-1 and maximal-scale interval discrepancy.

The oracle discrepancy-greedy ordering has a favorable finite cumulative proxy, but no deterministic ordering theorem is proved and the orbit of one seed b+tQ does not control the many distinct old seeds inside a short prefix without first paying Q.

The exact random-subset Fourier coefficient is product_q(1+chi(q))/2; exponential mixing would follow from a uniform prime-character gap at moduli p asymptotic to k. Such an unconditional input is not certified here, GRH would be conditional, and even perfect phase mixing does not supply the separate many-seed fixed-prefix transfer.
The elementary bad-phase divisor-counting lemma only guarantees avoidance of hQ congruent to small a for an initial O(m/(HA)) range of stages and cannot control the middle and late merges.
The proved pair-collision average sum_p(E_p-N)<=N(N-1)floor(log(H-1)/log k) becomes vacuous as soon as H>k because the number of remaining interval primes is less than k.

The proved additive large-sieve bound gives only N=O(H log k/k) for a macroscopic remaining set and therefore stalls after O(log k) old half-density constraints; the proved boundary-variation bound can accumulate with one sign over linearly many old blocks.

The exact coordinates p=k+a and n=2k+t give t mod p in [a+1,2a], while quotient layers leave gaps of length k/(q+2). Multiplying those gaps back by q+2 recovers exactly the original requirement that (n-k,n) contain no interval-prime multiple, so this is not yet an upper-bound compression.

The canonical absorber Q_A=binom(k+A,A) costs exp(o(k)) and gives the exact inverse-binomial step c_p=((-1)^A binom(p-k-1,A))^{-1}. Its finite-difference identities and the proved low inverse-phase counting lemma do not control the many-seed maximum gap at the natural log^2 k discrepancy scale.

A correlated inverse-binomial fixed-prefix gap bound with loss at most k^B(log k)^{Cm} times product p/(p-k) would imply n_k=exp(o(k)), but this sufficient bridge is open and is not recorded as a closed result.

The proved dense-seed signed block lemma sum_p (p/b)|D_p|^2<=(H-1+4k^2)N only selects a density-correct merge while N/H is at least about k log k/B^2; it cannot enter the exponentially sparse canonical history.

The one-frequency divisor bound cannot be upgraded merely by finite differences of (-1)^A binom(b-1,A), because hR_A(b)-a modulo k+b is exactly the fixed integer hQ-a. For the primal count one must also impose R<Q to exclude the identity a=hQ.

The exact coupled block Fourier coordinate contains the additional Vandermonde derivative F_B'(b): h_{p,a}=a(-1)^(A+r-1)(binom(b-1,A)F_B'(b))^{-1}. Controlling this varying-modulus product with signed cancellation is the remaining block problem.

The proved small-vector near-resonance lemma gives a nonzero global frequency within P_B/(L+1)^r of zero whose every local coordinate has size at most L. Hence canonical multiplication alone does not separate all high-support characters from the prefix pole; a signed support-stratified theorem is required.

The special CRT lattice has coordinate-hyperplane vectors and is not directly admissible in the product-norm sense. Symmetric Minkowski loses the one-sided orthant, while a generic m^{O(m)} positive-orthant loss has logarithm Theta(k), not o(k).

The former fixed-D support-correlation target is now refuted. For every proposed absolute C,D, an exact partial-fraction frequency built from a fixed bounded prime-cluster pattern of rank r>D gives an interval correlation Omega_r(k^(2r)), contradicting k^(r+D)C^r. The no-go concerns termwise support bounds, not cancellation between supports or Erdos 451 itself.

Rank three has an exact row formula on the 2D orbit j->(j(p2-p1) mod p2,j(p3-p1) mod p3). Slicing one coordinate turns the mixed term into a family of affine-phase lower-rank discrepancies with p2 different starting phases, so the common-start rank-two theorem has no simple tensor induction. The direct and absorbed routes share a phase-uniform discrepancy obstacle but retain different arithmetic slopes.

The exact k=70, p=137, q=139 witness has scaled correlation 11495874=0.95759 k^4/2. The proved coherent-row lower bound is Omega(k^4/Delta) when both offsets are macroscopic, so a k^3*C^2 rank-two bound is impossible along bounded-gap families; one global polynomial loss D>=2 is necessary.

Multiplying adjacent-pair rotation losses gives sum log(1+k/Delta_i) of order r log k even at ordinary logarithmic gaps, hence exp(Theta(k)) over final blocks. More decisively, the bounded-cluster resonance proves that any uniform rank-r termwise bound needs extra polynomial exponent D_r>=r, whose natural full-rank ledger is again exp(Omega(k)). A surviving direct route must use cross-support/global cancellation or other scale-dependent structure, not the refuted fixed-D absolute-value recursion.

For the canonical affine rank-three term, the exact partial-fraction identity separates the inverse-binomial/Vandermonde rational contribution from a global CRT carry: sum_i m_i(ell)/H_i + ell*R_S = nu(ell)/Q. The formula extends to every rank, but supplies no inequality because the Fourier product depends on the full local carry vector, not the scalar nu.

The guarded exact system k=22, A=2, Q=276, moduli (37,41,43) has M_3=8761532 and M_3/(k*max M_2)=40.58820368380091, strictly killing the constant-one bounded-factor tensor handoff. Its size is only 1.700069387957852*k^5, so a fixed polynomial loss D>=2 per dyadic block remains viable.

A direct fixed-pattern resonance at ell=epsilon*L moves under the canonical substitution s=Qt-(k+1) to the centered global frequency a=<Q*ell>_P; the translation changes only its Fourier phase. If QL-a is nonzero, P divides it and r*log k<=log(Q|L|+R) whenever |a|<=R.

For log|L|=o(k) and log R=o(k), the absorbed low-pole rank ledger k^r is exp(o(k)). For finitely many fixed patterns, the primes supporting |a|<=R number O(R*k*loglog(k)/log^3(k)), which is o(k/log k) only in the affordable range R=o(log^2(k)/loglog(k)). This does not sum their Fourier supports or survive an unproved iterative absorber update.

The polynomial radius needed to neutralize the old fixed-D lower bound is |a|>>k^(r-D), far beyond the proved divisor range. Maynard's theorem gives no distribution of binom(k+A,A) modulo the changing cluster product, so neither complete neutralization nor an affine cluster counterexample is proved for the canonical multiplier alone.

Allowing q=Q_0*u changes the conclusion for every fixed-rank bounded-diameter obstruction. For N=O_R(k) cluster supports and thresholds R_S=P_S/[k^D(log k)^(C|S|)], exact periodic counting gives at most (2 floor(R_S)+1)(U/P_S+1) bad multipliers per support. With D>=2 and polynomial U, the union of resonance-bad multipliers and multipliers sharing a remaining prime has density o_R(1).

A diagonal cutoff R_0(k)->infinity can be chosen with R_0 log k=o(k), C_{R_0}<=k^(1/4), and bounded-pattern Vandermonde constants below k. Then U=C_{R_0}(2k)^(R_0+4)=exp(o(k)) simultaneously moves every rank<=R_0 bounded-diameter cluster resonance beyond P_S/[k^D(log k)^(C|S|)] while preserving all remaining-prime inverses.

The free-multiplier lemma bounds only the known cluster character and its conjugate at O(2^r k^(r+D)(log k)^(Cr)). It does not bound other characters, arbitrary/high-rank supports, the cross-support signed sum, or the many-seed prefix transfer, and therefore does not prove an Erdos-451 upper bound.

Averaging q=Q_0*u over u<=U gives exactly a positive divisor-weighted count on s<=UH. For every subexponential U,H the actual full 451 conductor P is much larger than UH and the genuine full-support character a=1 has |B_P(1)|>=cos(pi/6)UH. Exact bilinear second moments and absolute support ledgers therefore do not close the interface: conductor-only pointwise decay, separated global Cauchy--Schwarz, and characterwise triangle summation are refuted as methods. A signed coupling of the inverse-binomial/Vandermonde Fourier coefficient with B_{P_S}(a) remains open.

Restricting u,t to units gives a distinct exact multiplicative-character diagonalization with principal density delta^times=product (p-k-1)/(p-1)=(1-o(1))D. Low-conductor complete-period cancellation is disrupted by the outer principal unit sieve and needs weighted character sums; full conductor P=exp(Theta(k)) lies beyond Burgess for U,H=exp(o(k)), while separated group L2 again costs exp(Theta(k)). The weighted coefficient--character-sum interface remains open.

For X=exp(gamma*k/log k) and fixed 0<eta<4/3, the exact primitive-conductor Mobius decomposition, Polya--Vinogradov, and the local coefficient ledger prove that every nonprincipal character of conductor f<=X^(4/3-eta) contributes o(delta*X^2) in aggregate, including the full outer unit sieve. This is a genuine unconditional low-conductor theorem but leaves conductors through P=exp((1+o(1))k).

The factor f^(1/2+o(1)) in the bulk local L1 coefficient ledger is sharp at exponent level: Parseval plus Polya--Vinogradov give c*sqrt(k)/log k<=sum_{psi nonprincipal}|rho_p(psi)|<=C*sqrt(k). Consequently termwise Burgess plus absolute conductor summation is strongest at the Polya--Vinogradov 4/3 threshold; higher Burgess moments worsen it.

Exact-full-support orthogonality shows that for any affordable multiset W of exp(o(k)) units represented below exp(o(k)), the support-wise kernel square norm is at least (1-o(1))*|W|*product_p(p-2). Its separately Cauchy--Schwarz ledger is exp((1/2+o(1))k) relative to the density main term. Small-prime multiplicative walks inherit this obstruction unless their product budget is exp(Omega(k)). These are method no-go results, not signed-error lower bounds.

The surviving high-conductor slice has the exact physical form sum_x product_{p in S}(1_{A_p^times}(x)-delta_p), with outside density factors. Generic bounded-cumulant or violation-parity truncations are refuted by the even/odd parity cube, so the remaining theorem must exploit the special 451 product multiset and retain the Q_0-dependent signed high-order centered correlations.

For the actual common-start sets, the exact local multiplier covariance is negative for g=-1 but is positive and asymptotic to 1/g for every fixed positive g on narrow offset blocks. More generally, any s<m fixed unit generators have a quadratic character trivial on every generator and supported on at least (m-s)/2 primes. Thus a generator-only uniform spectral contraction with s=o(m) is impossible; this is not an actual signed-error lower bound because the corresponding interval coefficients may vanish.

Positive dilation of an affordable prefix has total-variation boundary at least log(g)/log(gT), much larger than the survivor density, so complete-group contraction cannot be transferred by paying the boundary absolutely. Independently, on the macroscopic dyadic block 3k/2<p<2k, exact-support orthogonality and the product difference bound give a diagonal kernel of size exp((1/2+o(1))k); separated coefficient/kernel Cauchy--Schwarz therefore loses exp((1/4+o(1))k). Conditional cumulant expansion plus difference energy cannot absorb its full-order remainder without signed coupling.

The exact conductor heat transform H_W(sigma)=sum_chi f_chi^(-sigma)c_chi K_chi(W)=sum_x product_p(delta_p+p^(-sigma)z_p(x)) keeps coefficients, Q_0 phases, and the actual product kernel coupled. Its positive physical form is a weighted near-survivor enumerator. If no exact survivor exists, the bound using only one forced violation is H_W(sigma)<=N*sigma*log(2k). Therefore principal-scale positivity can certify a survivor by this handoff only for sigma*log k=O(delta), but then every f|P has f^(-sigma)=1-o(1). Conductor heat strong enough to damp high supports has insufficient endpoint resolution unless a new near-survivor theorem is supplied.

For y=Q_0*x, the squarefree triangular divisor D(y)=product_{j<k} gcd(y+j, product_{p>k+j}p) contains exactly the remaining primes at which x is allowed; equivalently p divides binom(y+p-k-1,p-k-1). Every centered support correlation is exactly kappa_S sum_x (-1)^omega(E_S) product_{p|E_S}(p-k-1)/k, where E_S=P_S/gcd(P_S,D(y)). This is a genuine signed shifted-divisor interface, but D(y)|product_{j<k}(y+j) gives only omega(D)=O(k^2/log^2 k), larger than the entire prime set by k/log k, so size-only divisor counting yields no cancellation or even a forced violation.

The missing-prime weight has the exact Mobius transform C_S=(-1)^|S| delta_S sum_{d|P_S} mu(d) E_d/delta_d, where E_d=N_d-delta_d*N and N_d has a signed bilinear character-square expansion with coefficient chi(-Q_0) product_p sum_{j<=p-k-1} conjugate(chi_p(j)). Even granting generic Type-II distribution through Q_0*X^2 at X=exp(gamma*k/log k), the visible support rank is at most (2gamma+o(1))k/log^2 k=o(|P|). For the actual failure probabilities q_p=k/(p-1)>1/2, every proper odd Bonferroni principal ledger is nonpositive. The independent high-rank remainder scale exceeds the survivor scale by exp((1+o(1))k/log k), so a separate asymptotic around that comparator needs exponential relative accuracy; only a Q_0-phase-preserving signed coupling of the low-rank ledger with the actual full-order remainder remains viable.

The exact violation polynomial is F_X(z)=N product_p(delta_p+q_p*z)+sum_T z^(m-|T|)(1-z)^|T| E_{P_T}. Every proper-degree multilinear pointwise one-sided endpoint certificate has nonpositive principal expectation, and two nonnegative rational laws have identical all proper marginals but endpoints 0 and 2*delta; a universal contour bridge also has condition number at least r^(-m). Thus the low-rank/full-remainder coupling cannot be closed distribution-freely. For fixed 0<eta<4/3, the precise remaining conditional lemma is the single full-modulus signed endpoint estimate over primitive conductors f_chi>X^(4/3-eta), with coefficient chi(-Q_0) product_p sum_{j<=p-k-1} conjugate(chi_p(j)) and complex kernel (S_X^P(chi))^2, at absolute scale o(delta*N). It is open and closes no campaign claim.

For real unit weights a_g, the shifted physical count has the exact phase-preserving form Z_a=sum_chi c_chi*A_a(chi)*(S_X^P(chi))^2, with principal term delta*N when sum a_g=1. A coefficient-aware high-conductor bound o(delta*N), together with log(sum|a_g|)=o(k/log k) and log(max g)=o(k), would conditionally yield n_k=exp(o(k)). However, affordable universal damping is refuted: sparse supports have a high-conductor quadratic character trivial on every multiplier value and on -Q_0, while any subexponential support/value/l1 multiplier has exact-full-support energy at least (1-o(1))*product_p(p-2)/S. Stable inversion pays reciprocal spectral cost. These are uniform/separated method no-go results, not a lower bound for the coefficient-weighted signed aggregate; no Erdos-451 claim is closed.
